content.content:
`deccy draft <node>... [--edit <id>]` opens one draft per named node, each created at its own workspace path, writes each draft's record `open`, and reports each draft's handle together with the workspace path that holds it. It does that and nothing else: the verb writes no graph state.

deccy is invoked as `deccy <verb> [args]` — one verb per invocation, a single lowercase word, and everything after it that verb's arguments (wzmmmmsw). So the surface is one verb, `draft`, with its own arguments: one or more node ids and an optional `--edit <id>`. Each purpose is served by exactly one verb and there are no aliases (znkxvuyv): opening a draft is served by `draft` and by no second spelling, and landing, recording, removing and reporting a draft are each a purpose of their own, so `draft` is not an alias for any of them. The argument surface is answered before the workspace is reached (qtqnuqxo): a verb answers its argument surface from any context and without waiting on a workspace, refusing by name an argument the form does not name and a required flag the call leaves out. This form's list is one or more node ids, so a call naming none is refused at that same point — before a workspace or a record exists, so a malformed call cannot leave half a draft behind.

The positional list is read through the draft model: a draft names exactly one node — the node whose content it will change — and the edit it belongs to; an edit carries a draft for each node it touches; a node may carry several drafts, within one edit as competing alternatives or across edits as a redraft; each draft is written in its own workspace; and landing is per draft (znskspqs). One draft per named node is that sentence read from the argument list: three ids are three drafts, each naming one node, not one draft spanning three. A node named twice is two drafts, because the model counts drafts rather than nodes and already allows a node several; the verb neither collapses nor deduplicates the list. Each draft belongs to exactly one edit — the one `--edit` names, or, when the flag is omitted, the edit the invocation is made in, the working copy's current edit — because a draft without an edit is not a draft the model has a place for (znskspqs) and a record names exactly one edit as a reference rather than deriving it from the node (owyntkvw). Opening a draft is an operation on a repository, since the node it names and the edit it belongs to are there, so a root-less call is refused once the surface has been answered (qtqnuqxo).

One workspace per draft is the same model read from the workspace side (znskspqs), and where that workspace is has already been answered: a draft's jj workspace is created under one per-user draft-workspace root outside the repository, at a path inside that root derived from the record's handle — the repository's own namespace under that root together with the handle (xqzstoyo). Two consequences follow, and both are this surface's. Because the path is derived from the handle and from nothing else, the verb mints the draft's handle before any directory can be named, and that is the same handle the record will carry as its key (owyntkvw). And because the path is derived, a call naming three nodes creates three workspaces at three derived paths, while two calls naming one node do not meet in one directory. xqzstoyo leaves the creation of a workspace, the jj name of one and the meaning of a missing one to the commitments that own them; this surface owns creating each draft's workspace, and it creates it at the path the handle derives, while the jj workspace's own name is not fixed here.

Writing the record is writing the first state of the record's life. A record has exactly two states, `open` for a draft that has not landed and `landed` for one that has; the only transition is `open` → `landed`, and it happens when the draft lands (vkkwusty). A draft the verb has just opened has landed nothing, so its record is written `open`, and `open` is not a default chosen from a menu but the only state the lifecycle offers a new draft. The record is minted for the draft: its identity is a handle generated for that draft and written into it as its key, so exactly one record exists per draft, and its node, edit and workspace are carried as references (owyntkvw). It is stored as exactly one JSON document at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, the filename the handle, in the untracked work-state registry (twpvqstu). So writing each record is writing one file per draft at the name the handle already gives: no allocation step, no index to keep in agreement, and no part of the draft's state kept anywhere else.

The report is the handle and the workspace path. The handle is the record's identity and the only thing that picks one draft out (owyntkvw); the workspace path is derived from that handle under the per-user root (xqzstoyo). A caller holding only the node and the edit cannot find the draft, because a node may be named by several records at once (owyntkvw), while a caller holding the handle can find both the record and the directory it names, because the path follows from the handle. Printing the pair as each draft is opened, in the order the nodes were named, is the smallest report that makes every draft the call opened reachable, and it reports the record's own fields rather than minting a second identity for the CLI to keep. The record still carries the workspace as a reference, and the report does not replace that reference with itself (owyntkvw).

The verb touches no graph state, and that clause is the three prerequisites about the record read together. The only durable thing the verb writes is each draft's record, and a record is not a node document: it is not `nodes/<id>.json`, it is not listed with the nodes and their edges, it is not validated as a node, and it is not attributed to a change, because attribution runs through node id and the record has none (owyntkvw). It is written into the untracked registry, so no change carries it and nothing about it is attributed to a change (twpvqstu). And opening does not move the record to `landed`: that transition happens when the draft lands, and landing is the recording of the draft's named edits into its node's change (vkkwusty) — a purpose of its own, served by its own verb (znkxvuyv). So the call creates no node, writes no `nodes/` document, draws no edge, records nothing into any change, and leaves every existing record's state where it was. The graph a caller reads before the call and after it is the same graph; the one thing added is a record and a workspace per named node, outside it.

These clauses are one commitment, not a list of features: the verb is `draft` alone (znkxvuyv) with the invocation's one-verb form (wzmmmmsw) and a surface answered before anything is reached (qtqnuqxo); the list is one draft per named node (znskspqs), each at the path its own handle names (xqzstoyo); each record is minted per draft (owyntkvw), stored as the one document its handle names (twpvqstu) and written `open` because opening is not landing (vkkwusty); the handle and the path are reported because nothing else leads back to the draft (owyntkvw, xqzstoyo); and no graph state is written because a record is not a node and opening is not landing (owyntkvw, twpvqstu, vkkwusty). Drop the handle from the report and the drafts the call opened cannot be found; drop one workspace per draft and the drafts of one call would share a working copy the model says they do not share; let opening write the graph and the verb becomes a creation verb for nodes, which is a different purpose belonging to a different verb (znkxvuyv). They answer one question — what does opening a draft do? — with one answer: for each node named, a record `open` and a workspace of its own, both reported, and nothing of the graph written.

Deliberately not here: the handle's format and how it is minted; the jj workspace's own name; the exact text, separator and stream of the printed lines beyond their naming the handle and the path; how a node id is resolved to a node, and what a call does when a named id names nothing, which belongs to reading the graph rather than to opening a draft; what a failed workspace creation or record write leaves behind; and any exit status. Each can change without touching what is settled here: one draft per named node, one workspace and one `open` record apiece, both reported, nothing of the graph written.
content.rationale:
The surface exists to open drafts, and each of the eight prerequisites already answers one part of what that means; this node adds the joining of them into one verb, and carries no clause that any of the eight would have to be changed to permit.

The form comes from the invocation shape: deccy is invoked as `deccy <verb> [args]`, one verb per invocation, single lowercase words, everything after the verb that verb's arguments (wzmmmmsw). So `draft <node>... [--edit <id>]` is one verb followed by its own arguments, and the node ids and the edit are this verb's arguments rather than a second verb's. One purpose is served by exactly one verb with no aliases (znkxvuyv), so opening a draft has exactly the spelling `draft`, and landing, recording, removing and reporting each have their own single verb — which is why this surface does not extend `draft` to perform them. The argument surface is answered before a workspace is reached: a verb answers its argument surface from any context, refusing by name an argument the form does not name and a missing required flag at the same point, while the operation the verb performs still refuses on a root-less context (qtqnuqxo). That is the licence for checking the node list and the edit before a workspace or a record is made, and for a root-less call being refused by the operation after the surface has answered.

What the list means comes from the draft model: a draft names exactly one node — the node whose content it will change — and the edit it belongs to; an edit carries a draft for each node it touches; a node may carry several drafts, within one edit as competing alternatives and across edits as a redraft; each draft is written in its own workspace; landing is per draft (znskspqs). One draft per named node is that sentence read from the argument list, and it is why the list is not deduplicated: the model counts drafts, not nodes, and already permits a node several. The edit reference is the other half of the same sentence, and the record carries exactly one edit as a reference (owyntkvw), which is why `--edit` names an edit rather than a node, and why an omitted flag falls back to the edit the invocation is made in instead of producing a draft with no edit.

The workspace is already placed, and this surface must respect the placement: a draft's jj workspace is created under one per-user root outside the repository, at a path inside that root derived from the record's handle — the repository's namespace plus the handle (xqzstoyo). Two things follow. The verb must mint the handle before it can name a directory, and that is the same handle the record carries as its key (owyntkvw), so the order is fixed at both ends without a naming step between them. And because the path is derived, one workspace per draft (znskspqs) is already one path per handle: the verb computes directories instead of choosing them, and two drafts opened by one call cannot collide. xqzstoyo itself declined to create a workspace, to name its jj workspace, or to decide what a missing one means, leaving those to the commitments that own them; this surface owns the creation, and its clause names only the path the handle derives.

What is written is fixed by the record and the store. Identity is a handle minted for the draft and written into the record as its key, exactly one record per draft, with exactly one node, one edit and the workspace carried as references (owyntkvw); the store holds one JSON document per record at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`, the filename the handle, in the untracked work-state registry (twpvqstu). A record per draft — not per call, not per node — is therefore the only thing the verb can write, and the write is one file at a name it already knows.

The state written is fixed by the lifecycle: two states, `open` for a draft that has not landed and `landed` for one that has, and the only transition `open` → `landed`, at landing (vkkwusty). A draft just opened has landed nothing, so `open` is not a choice among states but the only state a new record can have; and since the transition belongs to the landing, the verb cannot write `landed` without performing a landing that is not its purpose.

`Touching no graph state` is licensed by three of the eight prerequisites and by nothing outside them. owyntkvw licenses it from the record's side: the record is not `nodes/<id>.json`, not listed with the nodes and their edges, not validated as a node, and not attributed to a change, because attribution runs through node id and the record has none. twpvqstu licenses it from the store's side: the record is written in the untracked work-state registry, so no change carries it and nothing about it is attributed to a change. vkkwusty licenses it from the lifecycle's side: the state written is the non-landed one, and the landed one exists only after a recording — the move of a draft's named edits into its node's change — which opening does not make. Read together they say exactly the clause: the verb writes one file that no node listing, no change and no edge names, writes no `nodes/` document, records nothing into any change, and leaves every existing record where it stands. The clause is not a promise about side effects to be checked later; it is what the only object the verb writes already is.

The report is licensed by identity and derivation together: the handle is the record's key and the only thing that picks one draft out (owyntkvw), and the workspace path is derived from the handle under the per-user root (xqzstoyo). A caller told only the node and the edit cannot find the draft, because a node may be named by several records at once (owyntkvw); a caller told the handle can find both the record and the directory, because the path follows from the handle. Reporting the pair is the smallest report that leaves each opened draft reachable, and it reports the record's own fields rather than a second identity the CLI would have to keep.

What the decision is not: not a creation verb for nodes, not a landing verb, and not a second owner of where a workspace lives or how a record is stored. Those purposes belong to other verbs (znkxvuyv), and those placements belong to xqzstoyo and twpvqstu, which this node reads and does not revise. The licence from each of the eight is one licence: each already says what one part of opening a draft must look like, and the surface is their conjunction.
